question: Related Questions Q. Reading "Kimiya al-Sa'adat" Alchemy of Happiness 3834 views Q. Knowledge 6604 views Q. Ibn Arabi said, "العبد رب و الرب عبد" or "al-`abd-u rabb-un wa-r-rabb-u `abd-un" (the slave is the lord and the lord is the slave)." Sufis claim that such statements were always considered to be the most elevated exposition of mystical thought in Islam, and therefore unsuitable for the untrained mind. Ibn Arabi has also said, "الرب رب في التنزل والعبد عبد في الترقى" or "ar-rabb-u rabb-un f? t-tanazzul-i wa-l-`abd-u `abd-un f? t-taraqq?" (The lord is a lord in his descent [to his creations] and a slave is a slave in rising). in Fusoos Al-Hikam" and "Al-Ahkaam. answer: Miscellaneous >> Tasawwuf Question ID: 40715 Country: India Title: Reading "Kimiya al-Sa'adat" Alchemy of Happiness Question: I was about to read Imam Gazali’s "Kimiya al-Sa'adat" Alchemy of Happiness, translated version but some of my friends suggested that this book contains contents related to kufr and teaches about singing and dancing which are against the Shariah. Please guide me can I read this book by myself or I need guidance of some scholars as it is advised that reading books on Tasawwuf needs guidance of some scholar. Answer ID: 40715 Posted on: Sep 1, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 1668/1286/B=1433) You can read this book. It is very nice book for one’s inner purity. However, if you find any doubt or vagueness or some complication, then you should consult the Ulama. Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
